title: 2007 AMC 12A Problem 8
statement: A star-polygon is drawn on a clock face by drawing a chord from each number to the fifth number counted clockwise from that number. That is, chords are drawn from \(12\) to \(5,\) from \(5\) to \(10,\) from \(10\) to \(3,\) and so on, ending back at \(12.\) What is the degree measure of the angle at each vertex in the star-polygon?

solutions.text:
Consider the two chords meeting at the number \(5.\) They run to \(12\) and to \(10,\) so the arc they subtend extends from \(10\) to \(12.\)

That arc spans two of the twelve hour-marks, so its measure is \(\tfrac{2}{12}\cdot 360^\circ=60^\circ.\)

By the Inscribed Angle Theorem, the vertex angle is half the arc, or \(\tfrac12\cdot 60^\circ=30^\circ.\) By symmetry every vertex angle equals \(30^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Each vertex angle is an inscribed angle in the circle through the clock numbers
The two chords meeting at a vertex cut off an arc spanning two hour-marks, or \(60^\circ\)
